title: Grade 3 French — Mon, Jun 23
description: À l'école — Day 1 of 5: Classroom objects (les objets de la classe)
subject: french

questions.question: What is 'a pencil' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Un crayon' = a pencil. 'Un stylo' = a pen. 'Un livre' = a book. 'Une règle' = a ruler.

questions.question: What does 'un cahier' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Un cahier' = an exercise book or notebook. French students use 'un cahier' for their written work.

questions.question: How do you say 'a rubber/eraser' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Une gomme' = an eraser/rubber. 'Une colle' = glue. 'Un taille-crayon' = a pencil sharpener. 'Un feutre' = a felt-tip pen.

questions.question: What is 'un sac à dos'?
questions.explanation: 'Un sac à dos' = a backpack/school bag. 'À dos' literally means 'on the back.'

questions.question: Choose the correct French word for 'a ruler':
questions.explanation: 'Une règle' = a ruler. 'Un compas' = a compass (for drawing circles). 'Un rapporteur' = a protractor. 'Une trousse' = a pencil case.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Je range mes crayons dans ___.' (I put my pencils in ___)
questions.explanation: 'Une trousse' = a pencil case. 'Je range mes crayons dans une trousse.' = I put my pencils in a pencil case.

questions.question: 'Un tableau' in a French classroom refers to:
questions.explanation: 'Un tableau' = a blackboard or whiteboard. 'Le professeur écrit au tableau' = The teacher writes on the board.

questions.question: What is the gender (masculine/feminine) of 'règle', 'trousse' and 'cahier'?
questions.explanation: 'Une règle' (f), 'une trousse' (f), 'un cahier' (m). French nouns have grammatical gender — the article (un/une) shows it.

questions.question: Translate: 'I have a book and a pen.'
options: J'ai un livre et un crayon.
J'ai un livre et un stylo.
J'ai une règle et un stylo.
J'ai un cahier et une gomme.
questions.explanation: 'J'ai un livre et un stylo.' = I have a book and a pen. (livre = book, stylo = pen/biro).

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a classroom object?
questions.explanation: 'Un chien' = a dog — not a classroom object! 'Un cahier' = notebook, 'un stylo' = pen, 'une gomme' = eraser.

questions.question: 'Des crayons de couleur' means:
questions.explanation: 'Des crayons de couleur' = colour pencils / crayons. 'De couleur' means 'of colour.'

questions.question: How do you ask 'Do you have a rubber?' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Tu as une gomme ?' = Do you have a rubber/eraser? ('Tu as' = you have; 'une gomme' = a rubber).

questions.question: In French, 'les fournitures scolaires' means:
questions.explanation: 'Les fournitures scolaires' = school supplies / stationery — the collective term for all classroom objects (pencils, rubbers, books, etc.).

questions.question: Make the sentence plural: 'J'ai un stylo.' → ___
questions.explanation: Plural: 'J'ai des stylos.' (un → des in plural). 'Des' = some/the (plural indefinite article).

questions.question: Describe what is in your pencil case using French. Best answer:
options: Dans ma trousse, il y a un crayon, une gomme et un taille-crayon.
Ma trousse a crayon et gomme.
J'ai la trousse avec un stylo.
Une trousse il y a des crayons.
questions.explanation: 'Dans ma trousse, il y a un crayon, une gomme et un taille-crayon.' = In my pencil case, there is a pencil, a rubber and a pencil sharpener. This uses 'il y a' (there is/there are) correctly.
